bull.t: Product revenue growth and gross margin
bull.b: Rapid OneRF adoption and positive product gross profit show commercial traction. Sustained procedure growth could expand the revenue base and provide operating leverage, although the company must maintain margins while scaling.

Minimal debt reduces refinancing risk, interest burden and solvency pressure while the company funds commercialization. This gives management greater flexibility to direct resources toward products and regulatory milestones.

A major commercialization partner and progress toward ISO certification can broaden distribution beyond the current U.S. base. These capabilities may support international sales and improve the scalability of NeuroOne's platform.

bear.b: Revenue growth has not yet translated into sustainable profitability because operating expenses substantially exceed gross profit. Continued losses could limit investment capacity and require additional financing before scale benefits emerge.

Heavy cash consumption and a sharply lower cash balance create ongoing funding risk despite low debt. Reliance on equity issuance could dilute shareholders and leave growth plans dependent on capital-market access.

A revenue-recognition error weakens reporting confidence and highlights internal-control risk during commercialization. Delays in drug delivery, international rollout and other partnered programs also reduce visibility into durable revenue conversion.
